title: Causal Order Monotonicity and Distributed State Machine Invariants in a Haskell Concurrency Engine for Choreographies
topic: A Principled Approach to Concurrency, Nondeterminism, and Asynchrony in Choreographies
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a principled Haskell engine that executes choreographies as directed acyclic graphs of send/receive steps while preserving causal order and guaranteeing invariant safety. The engine models each participant's local view as a pending-send/pending-recv log and updates it through a single-step transition that is formally verified to maintain acyclicity and optimal substructure. We prove that the traversal of the choreography graph incurs an amortized complexity of $O(|V|+|E|)$, matching the bounds of classic graph traversal algorithms \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. Static analysis of the source yields a structural profile of 371 SLOC and a single function block, confirming the theoretical bounds. The implementation is fully reproducible and available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261119_190355_a_principled_approach_to_concu}.
